title: Decorators & Context Managers
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Decorators & Context Managers in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Decorator
items.text: A decorator is a callable that wraps another function or class to add or modify behavior.

items.heading: Decorator syntax
items.text: Putting @name above a function applies that decorator to the function.

items.heading: @property
items.text: @property is a built-in decorator that lets a method be accessed like an attribute.

items.heading: Wrapper function
items.text: A decorator often creates a wrapper function that runs extra code before or after the original function.

items.heading: functools.wraps
items.text: functools.wraps helps a wrapper preserve useful metadata such as the original function name and docstring.

items.heading: Common decorator uses
items.text: Decorators are often used for logging, authorization, caching, timing and validation.

items.heading: Context manager
items.text: A context manager controls setup and cleanup around a block of code. It is commonly used with with.

items.heading: with statement
items.text: with enters a context and ensures its cleanup behavior is performed when the block finishes.

items.heading: __enter__
items.text: A custom context manager can define __enter__() for setup and for the value returned after as.

items.heading: __exit__
items.text: __exit__ handles cleanup and receives information about an exception if one occurred.

items.heading: Safe resource handling
items.text: Context managers are useful for files, locks, database connections and other resources that need reliable cleanup.
